intro: Construction managers already lead people, budgets and schedules, which most management roles need. The closest of the 25 careers below is Industrial Production Managers, with an 84% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $126,060, or 10% more than the $114,990 construction managers earn.
why_it_works: Running a site means juggling crews, contractors, inspections and cost overruns. O*NET rates judgment and managing people at 4.12 out of 5 for this job, among the highest scores on any page. That is why production, facilities and operations managers match closely. Few matches pay more, since your pay is already high. New skills are more technical: programming, running equipment and selling ideas.
tips: Translate site work into plant language: safety records, throughput and schedule recovery show production readiness.
Purchasing is a natural fit: Purchasing Managers earn $148,080, which is 29% more, and use your contract skills.
If you are an engineer by training, check civil engineering roles at a 79% match, which earn $100,840.

faq.q: What jobs can former construction managers do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Industrial Production Managers (84%), General and Operations Managers (81%) and Facilities Managers (79%), based on O*NET 31.0. Facilities Managers earn $106,660, which is 7% less than the $114,990 construction manager median, but often bring steadier hours.

faq.q: Which careers for construction managers pay more?
faq.a: Only 3 of the 25 matches pay more. Computer and Information Systems Managers earn $175,140 (52% more), Purchasing Managers $148,080 (29% more) and Industrial Production Managers $126,060 (10% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Your pay is already high, so most moves are about the work, not a raise.

faq.q: Do construction managers need another degree?
faq.a: No. All 25 matches usually need no more education than construction managers already have. In the closest match, 29% of workers have a high school diploma as their highest level, so experience leading projects counts more than a new degree.

faq.q: What skills should construction managers learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are programming, operation and control, persuasion and repairing. Complex problem solving already rates 4 out of 5 for your job in O*NET, so the step is learning the technology and sales side of a new industry.
